claims.text: The initial material is as-cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr.
As-cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility.
Equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C.
Untreated HfNbTaTiZr has inadequate oxidation resistance for high-temperature use in air.
Low-temperature pack aluminizing will promote aluminum uptake at the HfNbTaTiZr surface.
Pack aluminizing will produce a thin, uniform, continuous, and adherent Al2O3 surface layer on HfNbTaTiZr.
The Al2O3 scale will act as a barrier to oxygen diffusion.
Restricting oxygen diffusion will limit oxygen ingress and oxidation of the underlying HfNbTaTiZr alloy.
Using a low-temperature aluminizing treatment will minimize changes to the bulk alloy microstructure.
Minimizing bulk microstructural changes will prevent degradation of mechanical performance.
Aluminized HfNbTaTiZr will show markedly lower oxygen uptake and oxidation-induced degradation than untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr at 1000 °C in air.
After aluminizing and oxidation exposure, the alloy will retain 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility.
After aluminizing and oxidation exposure, the alloy will retain a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C.
The proposed protection is applicable during exposure in air at approximately 1000 °C for 1–3 hours.
The proposed protection remains valid under mechanical loading at strain rates of 10^-4–10^-2 s^-1.
Aluminizing may induce unintended phase transformations if its process parameters are not adequately controlled.
High-temperature ductility degradation in this alloy family may involve grain-boundary precipitation rather than severe oxidation alone.
